WaFd Bank, a federally-insured Washington state chartered commercial bank formerly known as Washington Federal Bank
(the "Bank" or "WaFd Bank"), was founded on April 24, 1917 in Ballard, Washington and is engaged primarily in providing
lending, depository, insurance and other banking services to consumers, small, mid-sized and large businesses, and owners and
developers of commercial real estate. Effective September 25, 2025, the Bank formally changed its name from Washington Federal
Bank to WaFd Bank by filing its Second Amended and Restated Articles of Incorporation with the Washington Secretary of State.
WaFd, Inc., a Washington corporation, was formed as the Bank’s holding company in November, 1994. As used throughout this
document, the terms "WaFd," the "Company" or "we" or "us" and "our" refer to WaFd, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries, and
the term "Bank" or "WaFd Bank" refers to its bank operating subsidiary. The Company is headquartered in Seattle, Washington.
On November 9, 1982 the Company listed and began trading on the NASDAQ. Profitable operations have been recorded
every year since going public. As of September 30, 2026 , the stock traded at 81 times its original 1982 offering price, has paid 174
consecutive quarterly cash dividends and has returned 30,689% total shareholder return to those who invested 44 years ago.
On February 29, 2024, WaFd, Inc. closed its merger with Luther Burbank Corporation ("Luther Burbank" or "LBC"), a
California corporation, effective as of 12:00am on March 1, 2024. Pursuant to the LBC Merger Agreement, at the Effective Time
Luther Burbank merged with and into the Company (the “LBC Corporate Merger”), with the Company surviving the LBC
Corporate Merger. Promptly following the LBC Corporate Merger, Luther Burbank’s wholly-owned bank subsidiary, Luther
Burbank Savings, merged with and into WaFd Bank with WaFd Bank as the surviving institution (the “LBS Bank Merger”). The
LBC Corporate Merger and the LBC Bank Merger are collectively referred to in this Annual Report on Form 10-K as the “LBC
Merger.” The LBC Merger added approximately $7.7 billion of LBC assets at fair value to the Company's balance sheet, and the
Company assumed $50,175,000 in floating rate junior subordinated debentures, due June 2036 and June 2037, and $93,514,000 in
6.5% senior unsecured term notes which matured and were paid off on September 30, 2024. The LBC Merger expanded WaFd
Bank's footprint to nine western states with the addition of ten California branches of Luther Burbank.
On September 6, 2026, WaFd entered into a merger agreement (the “merger agreement”) with EverBank Financial Corp.
(“EverBank”), the bank holding company for EverBank, National Association, a diversified national bank headquartered in
Jacksonville, Florida. Subject to the terms and conditions set forth in the merger agreement, EverBank will merge with and into
WaFd, with WaFd continuing as the surviving corporation in the merger and electing to be treated as a financial holding company.
We refer to the merger with EverBank herein as the “EverBank Merger”, or the “merger”. Immediately following the EverBank
Merger, the surviving corporation will change its name to EverBank Financial Corp and WaFd’s wholly owned bank subsidiary,
WaFd Bank, will merge with and into EverBank’s wholly owned bank subsidiary, EverBank, National Association (the “EB Bank
Merger”), with EverBank, National Association continuing as the surviving bank in the EB Bank Merger.
If the EverBank Merger is completed, each share of EverBank common stock issued and outstanding immediately prior to the
effective time of the merger, other than certain shares as set forth in the merger agreement, will be converted into the right to receive
a number of shares of WaFd common stock equal to an exchange ratio determined as described below (the “exchange ratio,” and
such shares, the “merger consideration”). The exchange ratio will be determined in accordance with the merger agreement such that
immediately following the EverBank Merger:
• the former holders of EverBank common stock and EverBank equity awards will hold approximately 59.175% of the total
issued and outstanding shares of WaFd common stock on a fully diluted basis and
• the holders of WaFd common stock and WaFd equity awards (that are vested or will vest in the merger) will hold
approximately 40.825% of the total issued and outstanding shares of WaFd common stock on a fully diluted basis.
These ownership percentages are fixed and will not be adjusted for any reason, including any change in the trading price of
WaFd common stock. As of the date of this Annual Report on Form 10-K, WaFd estimates that approximately 107.3 million shares
of WaFd common stock, on a fully diluted basis, will be issued at the closing of the merger.
In addition, at the effective time of the EverBank Merger, each of the 675,000 outstanding shares of EverBank preferred
stock, each having a liquidation preference of $1,000 per share and bearing dividends at a fixed rate of 6.50% per annum, will be
automatically converted into the right to receive one share of a newly created series of preferred stock, par value $1.00 per share, of
WaFd having substantially equivalent terms as provided for in the merger agreement.
Holders of WaFd common stock will not receive any consideration in the EverBank Merger, and each share of WaFd
common stock and each share of WaFd’s 4.875% Fixed Rate Non-Cumulative Perpetual Preferred Stock, Series A will remain
issued and outstanding and will not be affected by the EverBank Merger.
The obligations of WaFd and EverBank to complete the EverBank Merger are subject to the satisfaction of various conditions,
including:
• approval of the issuance of the WaFd common stock pursuant to the merger agreement by WaFd shareholders;
• the WaFd common stock to be issued as merger consideration having been authorized for listing on Nasdaq, subject to
official notice of issuance;
• receipt of requisite regulatory approvals from the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, the Office of the
Comptroller of the Currency and the State of Washington, and the expiration of all statutory waiting periods in respect
thereof, and no such requisite regulatory approval resulting in the imposition of a materially burdensome regulatory
condition;
• the absence of any order, injunction, decree or other legal restraint preventing the completion of the EverBank Merger, the
EB Bank Merger or any of the other transactions contemplated by the merger agreement or making the completion thereof
illegal;
• with respect to each party, (a) the accuracy of the other party’s representations and warranties, subject to specified
materiality qualifications and (b) compliance by the other party with its obligations, covenants and agreements required to
be performed by it under the merger agreement in all material respects, and the receipt by each party of a certificate signed
on behalf of the other party by the chief executive officer or the chief financial officer to such effect; and
• the receipt by each party of an opinion of tax counsel that the merger will qualify as a “reorganization” within the meaning
of Section 368(a) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.
Neither WaFd nor EverBank can predict the actual date on which the EverBank Merger will be completed, or if the EverBank
Merger will be completed at all, because completion is subject to conditions and factors outside the control of WaFd and EverBank.
WaFd must obtain the WaFd shareholder approval, and WaFd and EverBank must also obtain the requisite regulatory approvals and
satisfy the other closing conditions. WaFd and EverBank expect the EverBank Merger to be completed promptly after those
approvals have been obtained and those conditions have been satisfied or waived. Subject to the satisfaction of the conditions to the
merger, the EverBank Merger is expected to close in early 2027.
The Company's fiscal year end is September 30th. All references herein to 2026 , 2025 and 2024 represent balances as of
September 30, 2026 , September 30, 2025 and September 30, 2024 , respectively, or activity for the fiscal years then ended.
The business of the Bank consists primarily of accepting deposits from the general public and investing these funds in loans of
various types, including construction loans, land acquisition and development loans, loans on multi-family, commercial real estate
and other income producing properties, and business loans, including U.S. Small Business Administration (“SBA”) loans. In
January, 2025, the Bank announced it will no longer originate consumer single family home loans and home equity lines of credit.

Ownership of our Common Stock involves risk. Investors should carefully consider, in addition to the other information
included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, the following risk factors. The risks described below may adversely affect our
business, financial condition and results of operations. These risks are not the only risks we face; additional risks and
uncertainties not currently known or that are currently considered to be immaterial may also materially and adversely affect
our business.
EverBank Merger Risks
Our ability to complete the EverBank Merger is subject to various closing conditions, including approval of the stock
issuance by WaFd shareholders and regulatory approvals, which may impose conditions that could adversely affect
WaFd or cause the merger not to be completed.
The EverBank Merger is subject to a number of conditions to closing as specified in the merger agreement. These
closing conditions include, among others, (a) the receipt of the WaFd shareholder approval, (b) the WaFd common stock to be
issued as merger consideration having been authorized for listing on Nasdaq, subject to official notice of issuance, (c) the
requisite regulatory approvals having been obtained and the expiration of all statutory waiting periods in respect thereof, (d) no
such requisite regulatory approval having resulted in the imposition of a materially burdensome regulatory condition, (e) the
absence of any injunction, order, decree or law preventing, prohibiting or making illegal the consummation of the merger, (f)
with respect to each party, (i) the accuracy of the other party’s representations and warranties, subject to specified materiality
qualifications, and (ii) compliance by the other party with its obligations, covenants and agreements required to be performed
by it under the merger agreement in all material respects, and the receipt by each party of a certificate signed on behalf of the
other party by the chief executive officer or the chief financial officer to such effect, and (g) the receipt by each party of an
opinion of tax counsel that the merger will qualify as a “reorganization” within the meaning of Section 368(a) of the Code.
No assurance can be given that the WaFd shareholder approval and regulatory approvals will be obtained or that the
other required conditions to closing will be satisfied. Even if regulatory approvals are obtained, no assurance can be given as to
the terms, conditions and timing of such approvals, including whether any required conditions will materially adversely affect
the combined company following closing. Any delay in completing the EverBank Merger could cause the combined company
not to realize, or to be delayed in realizing, some or all of the benefits that WaFd and EverBank expect to achieve if the merger
is successfully completed within its expected time frame. WaFd can provide no assurance that these conditions will not result in
the abandonment or delay of the EverBank Merger. The occurrence of any of these events individually or in combination could
have a material adverse effect on WaFd’s results of operations and the trading price of WaFd common stock.
The termination of the merger agreement could negatively impact our business or result in WaFd having to pay a
termination fee.
If the EverBank Merger is not completed by the termination date, either WaFd or EverBank may choose not to proceed
with the merger by terminating the merger agreement, and the parties can mutually decide to terminate the merger agreement at
any time, before or after the WaFd shareholder approval is received. In addition, WaFd and EverBank may elect to terminate
the merger agreement in certain other circumstances as further detailed in the section of the agreement entitled “The Merger
Agreement-Termination of the Merger Agreement.”
If the EverBank Merger is not completed for any reason, including as a result of a failure to obtain the WaFd
shareholder approval, our ongoing business may be adversely affected and, without realizing any of the expected benefits of
having completed the merger, we would be subject to a number of risks, including the following:
• We may experience negative reactions from the financial markets, including negative impacts on the price of WaFd
common stock;
• We may experience negative reactions from our customers, depositors and employees; and
• We will be required to pay our costs relating to the merger, such as financial advisory, legal and accounting costs and
associated fees and expenses, whether or not the merger is completed.
We will be required to pay EverBank a termination fee of $101,060,629 if the merger agreement is terminated by (a)
EverBank, prior to the receipt of the WaFd shareholder approval, because the WaFd board has made an adverse
recommendation change or because WaFd has materially breached its obligations relating to the proxy statement, the special
meeting, the WaFd board recommendation or the non-solicitation of acquisition proposals, (b) either party because the special
meeting has concluded without the WaFd shareholder approval having been obtained at a time when EverBank was entitled to
terminate the merger agreement for either of those reasons or (c) either party, without the WaFd shareholder approval having
been obtained, because the special meeting has concluded or because the EverBank Merger has not been completed by the
termination date, or by EverBank due to WaFd’s breach of the merger agreement, and, in each case under clause (c), (i) prior to
such termination a bona fide acquisition proposal had been publicly disclosed or announced or made known to our senior
management or the WaFd board and (ii) on or prior to the first anniversary of such termination, we consummate a transaction
with respect to an acquisition proposal or enter into a definitive agreement providing for such a transaction.
The announcement and pendency of the merger may adversely affect our business, financial results and operations.
Whether or not the merger is completed, the announcement and pendency of the merger could cause disruptions to our
business, including:
• Our current and prospective employees will experience uncertainty about their future roles with the combined
company, which might adversely affect our ability to retain key managers and other employees;
• uncertainty regarding the completion of the merger may cause our customers, depositors or others to delay or defer
certain business decisions or to decide to seek to terminate, change or renegotiate their relationships with WaFd, which
could negatively affect our revenues, earnings and cash flows;
